Six member delegation to visit Parliament street police station over Jantar Mantar curbs

Six member delegation to visit Parliament street police station over Jantar Mantar curbs

Heavy barricading at Jantar Mantar

NEW DELHI: A six member delegation comprising activists and politicians, including Neha, Prashant Bhushan, Yogendra Yadav, Nandita Narain, RJD leader Manoj Jha and Nikhil Dey, is scheduled to visit the Parliament Street Police Station in Delhi at 3 pm on Monday over restrictions on protests at Jantar Mantar.The delegation is seeking clarification from authorities on the reasons behind the alleged restrictions and the legal basis for them.In a statement announcing the visit, the delegation questioned why the right to protest at Jantar Mantar was being restricted and asked authorities to clarify the reasons for the decision.“For what reasons? By which Law? On whose orders?” the statement asked.The delegation also linked the issue to concerns over voting rights, asking: “Why is our Right To Protest At Jantar Mantar Being Snatched Along With Our Voter Rights?”Jantar Mantar in Delhi was heavily barricaded on September 25 amid nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Security personnel were also deployed outside the Election Commission office in New Delhi ahead of a Delhi Congress demonstration over the SIR exercise.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said on Friday that his organisation would launch nationwide protests from October 2 if Kumar did not resign by Saturday.
Article Summary: Six member delegation to visit parliament street police station over jantar mantar curbs. Delegation is seeking clarification from authorities on the reasons behind the alleged restrictions and the legal basis for them. The delegation also linked the issue to concerns over voting rights, asking: “why is our right to protest at jantar mantar being snatched along with our voter rights?”

Article Title: Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex crashes over 1,000 points, investors lose Rs 6 lakh crore - top reasons for fall
Article Text:
Both indices crashed over 1% amid the intensifying Iran-US conflict.

Why is stock market crashing today?

Iran-US conflict escalates

Oil prices jump

Bond yields soar

Rupee tumbles

FII outflows

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 , the Indian equity benchmarks tanked in morning trade on Monday as persistently high crude oil prices and a spike in US bond yields added to investors’ woes. Both indices crashed over 1% amid the intensifying Iran-US conflict.While Sensex crashed over 1,000 points, Nifty50 went below 22,850. At around 12:18 PM, Nifty50 was trading at 22,833.75, down 307 points or 1.33%. BSE Sensex was at 72,936.39, down 959 points or 1.30%.The selloff also erased nearly Rs 6 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies, taking it down to around Rs 476 lakh crore.Also Read | Two years ago Sensex hit lifetime high: What went wrong after that & what’s the road ahead? Every one of the 30 Sensex stocks was trading in negative territory. Bajaj Finance, Kotak Mahindra Bank and HDFC Bank led the decline. The weakness was not restricted to large-cap stocks. The Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 indices also declined by more than 1% each.Indian equities were also tracking the broader weakness across several Asian markets, where stocks came under pressure amid the surge in oil prices.South Korea’s Kospi declined more than 2%, while China’s Shanghai Composite dropped over 1.7%. Japan’s Nikkei, however, posted muted gains.Tensions between Iran and the US intensified after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire along with the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.Speaking to reporters on Saturday, Trump said, "I reject this agreement. They want an agreement to be made under which the Strait of Hormuz is immediately opened, because they are severely failing.”Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, said the country would remain firm and would not back down in the face of the US and Israel.The latest developments in the Middle East triggered another sharp rise in crude prices, with oil gaining 2% and moving close to $107 per barrel as markets factored in the possibility of further disruption to shipments. JPMorgan said it could no longer clearly assess where oil prices were headed and, for the first time since the Iran war began in February, said it did not have a defined baseline scenario for the market.US bond yields continued their climb, reaching fresh multi-year highs and adding another layer of pressure on equities. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note moved further above 5.2%, its highest level since 2004. The 30-year US bond yield also crossed 5.5%, while the yield on two-year Treasury notes, which generally moves alongside expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes, rose above 4.9%.Higher bond yields generally increase the attractiveness of debt markets for investors, which can put additional pressure on riskier assets such as equities.The Indian rupee weakened by 14 paise to 95.89 against the US dollar in early trading. Forex traders are increasingly concerned about the currency breaching the psychologically important 96 level against the dollar, with the rupee facing pressure from elevated oil prices, higher US Treasury yields and a stronger dollar.“Volatility in crude and gold, along with a rise in the dollar, limited the rupee’s ability to sustain gains. Going ahead, currency movement is likely to remain range-bound amid global commodity and dollar volatility. Rupee range can be seen between 95.50-96.50,” said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities.Foreign investors continued to sell Indian equities on Friday, offloading shares worth a net Rs 3,694 crore, according to provisional NSE data.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, said the shift in FPI flows towards the negative side after positive inflows in July and August had become visible earlier this month. He said the selling trend has continued, with total equity outflows through exchanges reaching Rs 25,682 crore so far this month.
Article Summary: Both indices crashed over 1% amid the intensifying iran-us conflict. Bajaj finance, kotak mahindra bank and hdfc bank led the decline. The selloff also erased nearly rs 6 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of bse-listed companies. Foreign investors continued to sell indian equities on friday, offloading shares worth a net rs 3,694 crore.

Dalal Street began the week on a negative note, with BSE Sensex tumbling over 1% and NSE Nifty50 trading below the 22,900 mark. Article Title: Balakot to Sindoor, India gave befitting reply: PM Modi on Pakistan terror
Article Text:
PM Modi’s stern message to Pakistan: ‘Time for sponsoring terror to go unpunished is long gone’

'Zero-tolerance terror policy has borne results'

NEW DELHI: In a stern message to Pakistan, PM Modi said on Sunday the time when its role in sponsoring terror attacks on India would go unpunished is long gone, and his govt has made it clear with its actions, including Op Sindoor, that terrorists will be given a befitting response for their sinister designs against India.Modi's message came in his 'Mann ki Baat' broadcast as India marks the 10th anniversary of the surgical strikes on terror hideouts in Pakistan on Sept 28-29, 2016. "The world was astonished to see the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the LoC to take action against terror. The strike demonstrated a new aspect of India's counter-terror policy. It was our decisive response to long-standing pain India had endured," he said."Over the past decade, from Balakot airstrike to Op Sindoor, India has repeatedly sent out a clear message: if terrorists dare to cast an evil eye on India, they will be met with a befitting response."Contrasting his government's targeted action against Pakistan to the approach of the previous Congress-led UPA govt, PM Narendra Modi said serial blasts had once become a common occurrence in the country. On Sept 13, 2008, serial blasts rocked Delhi and, just a few weeks later, the Mumbai terror attack stunned the country, the PM said.Demands for action against Pakistan following every terror attack used to be made then but were ignored. "Today, India pursues a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, and we are witnessing the results of that," he said.During Op Sindoor, the Modi govt also unveiled a tougher national security doctrine, declaring that any future terror attack will be treated as an act of war. This eliminated the false distinction between terrorists and their state sponsors, it had said.Modi's message to Pakistan comes at a time when the nation is trying to airbrush its long association with terror incidents around the world, reflected in its PM Shehbaz Sharif's recent claims at the United Nations General Assembly about its role and sacrifices in combating terrorism.In his UNGA address, foreign minister S Jaishankar had snubbed Pakistan, calling it a "serial practitioner of terrorism" and asserting that India will continue to exercise its right to defend itself against terror threats.
Article Summary: Pm modi's message came in his 'mann ki baat' broadcast as india marks the 10th anniversary of the surgical strikes on terror hideouts in pakistan on sept 28-29, 2016. "the world was astonished to see the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the loc to take action against terror," he said.

Article Title: Why are gold prices crashing today? MCX Gold down Rs 3,200/10 grams, plunges over 2% - top reasons for fall
Article Text:
Gold remains under pressure as both bond yields and crude oil prices moved higher.

Why is gold crashing today?

What’s the outlook?

How should you trade gold?

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Gold price crash today: The start of the week saw both the precious metals, MCX Gold and MCX Silver, crash on Monday as the rise in oil prices fuelled inflation worries and increased expectations that the US Federal Reserve could raise interest rates further.On the domestic bourse, MCX silver futures for September 2026 delivery fell Rs 6,661 to Rs 2,28,035 per kg. Gold futures for October 2026 delivery declined Rs 3,214 to Rs 1,47,667 per 10 grams.In international markets, spot gold was down 1.5% at $4,223.95 per ounce as of 0117 GMT, while US gold futures declined 1.5% to $4,257.90.Other precious metals also traded lower. Spot silver fell 2.6% to $62.64 per ounce, platinum declined 2.1% to $1,741.45 and palladium dropped 2.1% to $1,239.95.Gold remains under pressure as both bond yields and crude oil prices moved higher. The increase in oil prices, driven by mixed indications on supply flows, kept inflation risks firmly in focus among investors.Iran said diplomacy remained the only route to resolving its conflict with the United States and Israel. This came after US President Donald Trump said he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and bring the fighting to an end.Oil prices later recovered more than 1%.According to experts, the primary reason for prices falling sharply is the rise in US bond yields.Ashish Rajodiya, Head – Commodities, PL Capital says, “MCX Gold (December contract) is trading at Rs 1,50,500 per 10 grams, down Rs 2,700 or 1.80% today, extending its slide for a second straight week. The pressure is coming from a sharp US Treasury bond selloff - the 10-year yield at 5.13%, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year at 5.44%, its highest since 2004.”CME FedWatch data indicates that markets are now pricing a 68.1% probability of another 25 basis points rate hike by the US Federal Reserve in its October-end meeting. Earlier, the odds were just 31.9%.“Elevated crude prices, rather than boosting gold's safe-haven appeal as they typically would during geopolitical stress, are instead reinforcing the case for further Fed tightening, feeding a stronger dollar and steeper yield curve that both work against non-yielding bullion,” he says.Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities explains, “Global commodities are trading under pressure, with precious metals under sharp pressure as crude remains firm. Uncertainty around the US-Iran conflict continues to keep risk sentiment volatile. Recent diplomatic efforts have produced mixed signals, with Iran indicating readiness for both negotiations and renewed conflict, while the US has rejected Iran’s latest proposal, although further talks through mediators remain possible. ”“Gold is trading at $4185, down more than 2.%, and it is facing sharp selling pressure as geopolitical uncertainty, a firm Dollar and higher bond yields with 5.22% on 10yrs weigh on bullion as higher probability of rate hike prices in. The lack of clarity over a potential US-Iran settlement is keeping safe-haven demand volatile,” he adds.Ashish Rajodiya is of the view that gold prices have support at Rs 1,48,000 and Rs 1,46,000, with resistance at Rs 1,52,500 and Rs 1,55,000.“The metal's next move likely hinges on two threads converging at once: the Fed's October rate decision, and whether the recent signs of renewed US-Iran diplomatic engagement on Hormuz firm up into an actual de-escalation,” he says.“A dovish surprise from the Fed or confirmed progress on Iran talks could spark a sharp bounce toward resistance, while continued hawkish signals or a stalled Iran negotiation would likely extend the slide toward the lower support band,” he adds.Manoj Kumar Jain of Prithvi Finmart expects gold and silver to see continued volatility this week as traders track movements in crude oil prices and the dollar index, along with geopolitical tensions and developments in the US-Iran peace talks.For gold, he sees support at $4,284-4,260 per troy ounce, with resistance placed at $4,355-4,388. In silver, support is at $63.80-63.00 per troy ounce, while resistance stands at $65.50-66.60.On the MCX, Jain has identified support for gold at Rs 1,50,150-1,49,600 and resistance at Rs 1,51,400-1,52,000. For silver, his support levels are Rs 2,33,000-2,30,400, with resistance at Rs 2,36,600-2,38,800.Jain told ET that investors should wait for further developments in the US-Iran peace talks before initiating fresh positions in gold and silver. For those already holding long positions, he recommended keeping a strict stop-loss below Rs 1,49,600 for gold and below Rs 2,30,000 for silver, based on daily closing levels.

Article Title: Higher EPF wage limit: Monthly PF contributions rise to Rs 3,917
Article Text:
EPFO wage ceiling hike

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With EPFO increasing the mandatory wage ceiling from Rs 15,000 a month to Rs 25,000, employees will now contribute Rs 3,000 (at 12% contribution of Rs 25,000 wage) towards their PF savings from Rs 1,800 earlier, govt said in a set of FAQs released. This will be along with a contribution of Rs 917 by employers (at 3.67%), up from Rs 550, taking the mandatory monthly PF contributions to Rs 3,917.In addition, Rs 2,083 - an 8.3% contribution from employers' share - will now go towards the pension kitty from earlier Rs 1,250. On Sept 17, govt increased EPFO wage ceiling to bring one crore additional workers into the social security net as minimum wages in at least seven states and UTs - Delhi, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Haryana, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand - have crossed the Rs 15,000 threshold.In the case of an employee with a monthly wage of Rs 20,000, the mandatory PF contribution will be Rs 3,134 - the employee share Rs 2,400 and the employer share Rs 734, with an additional Rs 1,666 going towards EPS from employer's share. But if an employee earns, say, Rs 35,000 a month, the mandatory PF contribution will be Rs 6,000 (Rs 3,000 from employee and employers each), with no amount going towards pension as EPS is available only to those whose wages do not exceed the EPFO wage ceiling.The retirement savings agency said the new regime kicked in from Sept 17 and asked employers to review contractor compliance, wherever contract labour is engaged, and update its payroll systems.Allaying employee fears of attempts to pass on the contribution by deducting more from salaries, it said an employer's statutory contribution cannot simply be treated as an employee deduction merely by describing it as part of CTC.While the move will likely increase compliance costs for small and medium enterprises, the potential costs due to the rise in the wage ceiling can be partly offset by the incentive of up to Rs 3,000 per month for every additional employment created under PM Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana.
Article Summary: Epfo increasing mandatory wage ceiling from rs 15,000 a month to rs 25,000. Employees will now contribute rs 3,000 towards their pf savings from rs 1,800 earlier. This will be along with a contribution of rs 917 by employers (at 3.67%), up from rs 550.

Article Title: ‘Beating his drum away’: Congress targets PM Modi for ‘ignoring’ rising inflation in Mann Ki Baat
Article Text:
Cong targets PM Modi for 'ignoring' inflation

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not addressing rising inflation in his Mann Ki Baat radio address, accusing him of being “blissfully unconcerned” about the issue.The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat.“The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away. Vegetables are getting more expensive by the day, with onion prices soaring 48.27% in August. Items such as air conditioners, TVs and refrigerators are also set to become more expensive. Household savings are steadily declining, while family debt is mounting. In such a scenario, how is the common family supposed to meet its needs?” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X.Ramesh questioned why PM Modi continues to “sermonise” in the Mann Ki Baat series instead of addressing the public’s concerns.“In his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio series, the Prime Minister keeps sermonising on various issues, but when will he address the country’s most pressing concern—inflation? When will he care about the public’s worries? The public is already beleaguered by rising prices, and there’s no relief coming from the government.How on earth is the average family supposed to manage its budget? How long will the middle class and the poor have their backs broken like this?” the Rajya Sabha MP asked.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, retail inflation, based on the 2024=100 CPI, stood at 4.82% in August, up from 4.45% in July. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), rose to 5.95% in August from 5.52% in July. The August figures are provisional.Official data showed that onion inflation surged from 22.54% in July to 48.27% in August. Ginger recorded inflation of 73.82%, while garlic inflation stood at 43.60%. In contrast, tomato prices fell 31.09% year-on-year, while potato prices declined 13.14%.MoSPI data showed inflation in the combined food and beverages category at 5.66% in August. Transport inflation stood at 4.60 percent, education services at 3.73%, while restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 8.38%. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 15.17%.The CPI data was compiled from price information collected across 1,407 urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages nationwide. MoSPI reported a 100% response rate from both rural and urban markets in August.According to MoSPI, the next CPI data, covering September, is scheduled to be released on October 12.
Article Summary: Cong targets pm modi for 'ignoring' inflation in his mann ki baat radio address. Opposition party’s attack came a day after pm modi addressed the nation. Food inflation, measured by the consumer food price index (cfpi), rose to 5.95% in august.

Article Title: India to join SCO national coordinators meeting in Islamabad
Article Text:
Pakistan to host SCO coordinators’ meet from Sept 28-30

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India will participate in a meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) national coordinators that Pakistan will host on September 28-30, official sources said. The meeting is expected to approve the calendar of events under Pakistan’s presidency, leading up to the Council of Heads of State (CHS) summit for which Islamabad will soon send out invitations to the leaders of all member-states of the Eurasian bloc, including PM Narendra Modi.After joining the China-dominated grouping in 2017 as a full member, India has participated actively in various SCO mechanisms, with Modi representing India at the heads of state summits and external affairs minister S Jaishankar joining the heads of government meetings.Unlike with SAARC, India has ringfenced its involvement in SCO from outstanding bilateral differences with Pakistan, mainly the core issue of cross-border terrorism, while consistently reminding the Organisation that one of its original mandates was to fight terrorism, extremism and separatism. Government has backed SCO connectivity initiatives too but with the rider that these must respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States.India’s national coordinator Alok Dimri is expected to participate in the national coordinators’ meeting that will begin on Monday. Even without any substantive bilateral engagement for a decade, India and Pakistan have regularly seen their officials visiting each other’s country for SCO-related exercises and Jaishankar himself travelled to Pakistan in 2024 for the SCO heads of government meeting.However, the key question remains – even if it’s too early to ask – whether Modi will attend the summit in Islamabad next year. The SAARC summit process remains blocked because of the PM’s reluctance to travel to Pakistan and, barring a dramatic change in the situation, the PM is unlikely to visit Islamabad.According to Indian officials, any such change can only be effected by Islamabad through tangible and irreversible action against cross-border terrorism and UN-proscribed terror entities operating out of Pakistan. Government recently denied strongly that it is involved even in any track 2 dialogue with Islamabad.Pakistan had assumed presidency of the SCO at the Bishkek summit earlier this month. Modi said the same day in his address that countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy, providing shelter to terrorists, must be categorically told terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone.
Article Summary: Pakistan to host sco coordinators’ meet from sept 28-30. Meeting is expected to approve the calendar of events under pakistan’s presidency. Islamabad will soon send out invitations to the leaders of all member-states of the eurasian bloc.

Article Title: IndiGo A321 suffers tail strike in Bengaluru
Article Text:
An IndiGo A321 operating flight 6E 6542 from Guwahati to Bengaluru suffered a tail strike while aborting its landing on Sunday.

NEW DELHI: In yet another instance of an IndiGo Airbus A321 tail strike, an aircraft (VT-NHP) operating a Guwahati-Bengaluru flight Sunday suffered one while going around at its destination.Flight 6E 6542 aborted landing in its first approach. While making an ascent, it suffered a tail strike. The aircraft landed safely in its second attempt. DGCA has launched a probe.An IndiGo spokesperson said the flight experienced "abnormal runway contact" while landing during gusty weather at Kempegowda International Airport, adding, "All customers and crew are safe... All relevant authorities were info-rmed and the aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks."
Article Summary: An indigo a321 operating flight 6e 6542 from guwahati to bengaluru suffered a tail strike while aborting its landing on sunday. The aircraft landed safely in its second attempt. Dgca has launched a probe.

Six American F-35 fighter jets, along with more than 200 US airmen touched down in Jodhpur on Saturday to take part in the second edition of multinational air exercise, Tarang Shakti.US Ambassador Sergio Gor announced their arrival in his post on X, informing first ever American participation in the exercise.Gor said he looked forward to see American firth-generation fighters planes flying alongside the Indian jets.The second edition of Tarang Shakti got underway at Air Force Station Jodhpur in Rajasthan on Saturday, with more than 40 countries taking part in the drills.In a post on X, the Indian Air Force extended a welcome to the participating contingents, saying, "A warm welcome to our friends from across the skies as they touch down at Jodhpur. Article Title: IndiGo A321 suffers tail strike during go around at Bangalore; plane lands safely in second attempt
Article Text:
(Representative Image): IndiGo spokesperson said 6E 6542 “experienced an ‘abnormal runway contact’ while landing during gusty weather at Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru. All customers and crew are safe and have disembarked safely.

NEW DELHI: In yet another instance of an IndiGo Airbus A321 tail strike, an aircraft (VT-NHP) operating a Guwahati-Bengaluru flight on Sunday suffered the same while going around at its destination. The flight (6E 6542) aborted landing on the first approach at the destination. During ascent, it suffered a tail strike. The aircraft landed safely on the second attempt. The DGCA is probing this latest tail strike.IndiGo spokesperson said 6E 6542 “experienced an ‘abnormal runway contact’ while landing during gusty weather at Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru. All customers and crew are safe and have disembarked safely. In line with standard operating procedures, all relevant authorities were informed, and the aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks. It will resume operations after securing necessary clearances. As always, the safety of our customers and crew is our top priority.”The DGCA has raised this issue with IndiGo, and the airline has told it that the focus on pilot training for this particular area has been enhanced.About a year back, they used to happen mostly during landings. Now they are seen more during go-arounds. Airbus itself says, “There is also a higher risk of tail strike when a go-around is required near the ground.”UK’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau says the “rate of tail strike incidents per aircraft landing for the A321 is four times greater than that for the A320, probably as a result of the smaller margin from the normal flare attitude. Damage to the structural integrity of the fuselage should not pose a significant flight risk to the aircraft provided the tail strike is detected during or after landing.”An Airbus publication on safety says: “Performing a go-around near the ground is a very dynamic phase with a risk of tail strike. If a go-around is initiated, the (required) manoeuvre must be completed. Between Jan 2022 and Sept 2024, 49 tail strike events were reported to Airbus, with five (10%) during takeoff, 23 (47%) during landing and 21 (43%) during a go-around near the ground.”Tail strikes are a global phenomenon. According to the International Air Transport Association (IATA) Safety Report, tail strikes were the most frequent type of incident in 2024 and in 2025, although fatality risk remains low. IATA data shows tail strikes were the most frequent non-fatal incidents globally at nine, followed by landing gear issues at seven and runway excursion at six.“The ATR 72 and Boeing 737NG (-800/-900ER) were most frequently involved, accounting for 46% of events. Most tail strikes occurred during landing (69% when including rejected landings). Asia Pacific recorded the highest number of events, with the US, India, and Brazil among the most affected countries,” says the IATA Annual Safety Report - 2025.
Article Summary: Indigo spokesperson said 6e 6542 ‘experienced an ‘abnormal runway contact’ while landing during gusty weather at kempegowda international airport, bengaluru. All customers and crew are safe and have disembarked safely. The aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks.

Article Title: 'Will never bow our head': Iran embassy invokes Baahubali to echo Pezeshkian's defiant UN speech
Article Text:
The post follows Pezeshkian's address at the 81st UNGA in New York on September 23, where he rejected the prospect of Iran surrendering to US pressure.

In a dramatic blend of cinema and diplomacy, the Iranian Embassy in Hyderabad has drawn a parallel between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's defiant address at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) and the iconic battle scenes from the Telugu blockbuster Baahubali. The embassy shared a video featuring the film's protagonist taking on the enemy army, accompanied by a message asserting Iran's determination to stand firm against external pressure.The video features scenes from Baahubali: The Beginning, in which Amarendra Baahubali, played by Prabhas, leads his forces against the Kalakeya army."Dr. Pezeshkian, President of Islamic Republic of Iran at UNGA: 'Will never bow our head or bend the knee' Like Baahubali standing against the Kalakeyas, we also shed our own blood in sacrifice for the homeland," the embassy wrote alongside the video.The comparison draws on one of the film's most memorable sequences, in which Baahubali refuses to retreat despite facing a formidable enemy.The post follows Pezeshkian's address at the 81st UNGA in New York on September 23, where he rejected the prospect of Iran surrendering to US pressure. Responding to US President Donald Trump's remarks a day earlier, Pezeshkian said that sanctions, pressure and threats would only strengthen the Iranian people's resolve."We will never bow our head or bend at the knee," he declared, while also expressing Iran's willingness to pursue dialogue and diplomacy without accepting coercion.Pezeshkian's speech came amid escalating tensions between Iran and the United States.He accused Washington and Israel of attacking Iranian territory and defended his country's military response, while maintaining that Tehran remained open to negotiations. He also criticised sanctions and raised concerns about civilian casualties and the conflict in West Asia. These remarks formed the backdrop to the embassy's subsequent social media post.
Article Summary: The iranian embassy in hyderabad has drawn a parallel between iranian president masoud pezeshkian's defiant address at the united nations general assembly (unga) and the iconic battle scenes from the telugu blockbuster baahubali.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has again trained his guns at the Election Commission . Reviving his allegations about the conduct of the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, he said the votes of SP supporters were deliberately deleted. His latest attack comes amid the ongoing controversy over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.Akhilesh said that the alleged malpractice was not new. He said it had been taking place for years and has only been exposed now."This malpractice has been going on all along; the only difference now is that it has been exposed," he said.The SP chief also went back to the 2022 election. He alleged that the Election Commission and officials had worked together to delete votes belonging to the Samajwadi Party.He said, "We didn't pay enough attention in 2017. We trusted and believed that the Election Commission would be impartial and would not compromise its credibility."He added that his concerns became clear after the 2022 Assembly election results, saying, "When the results came out in 2022, I remember stating at our national convention that the Election Commission and officials had colluded to deliberately delete the votes of the Samajwadi Party.”Akhilesh further alleged that people who had voted in the 2019 elections were subsequently prevented from voting in 2022."Those who had voted in 2019 were denied the opportunity to vote in 2022—without notice and without adherence to any rules or laws—and the result was that a Samajwadi government was not formed in 2022," he said.His latest remarks come against the backdrop of the continuing political row over the Election Commission's SIR exercise after a report by Indian Express revealed objections raised by two of the three election commissioners for the revision.Opposition parties have since raised concerns over the revision of electoral rolls and the possibility of eligible voters being left out.

Article Title: 'Wrong message to society': Rijiju attacks Rahul Gandhi over Gyanesh Kumar resignation demand
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi had alleged that the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were “all rigged”.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Sunday attacked leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his criticism of the Election Commission and demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, saying such remarks would send a “wrong message to society”.Speaking to reporters, Rijiju said, “It is not appropriate to amplify Rahul Gandhi's remarks in the public sphere, as it would send the wrong message to society.”His remarks came days after Rahul Gandhi stepped up his attack on the Centre and the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Rahul had alleged that the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were “all rigged” and demanded the immediate resignation of Gyanesh Kumar.Addressing a press conference at the Congress headquarters on Thursday, the Congress leader accused the Election Commission of failing to protect voters’ rights and alleged that the electoral process had been compromised.“Mr Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately. We are not going to let democracy be destroyed in India and sit silent, and the people responsible for this are going to be punished,” the Rae Bareli MP said.Rahul also referred to reports that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections on several occasions over decisions related to electoral-roll management and the SIR exercise.“The two Election Commissioners have done a wise thing, and I appreciate it,” he said. Rahul further alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were “at the top of this conspiracy” and would be investigated. He also said Kumar should “turn approver”.“I can say with certainty that Indian elections -- 2024 Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha polls -- were all rigged,” Rahul said. He also linked his allegations over electoral rolls to the functioning of Parliament and other institutions.“From vote chori (vote theft), comes kanoon chori (law theft) and from that comes sanstha chori (institutional theft),” he said.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that the reported objections reflected a disagreement over its final decisions.The poll panel said on Saturday that key decisions related to the SIR, including orders and schedules, were taken with the “unanimous approval” of all three commissioners.It also clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary, which had drawn scrutiny, concerned the functioning of an officer on deputation to the ECI and was not related to any policy matter, ANI reported.The clarification came after an Indian Express report said that Sandhu and Joshi had formally raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months on issues including voter registration, deletion and restoration of names, changes to Form 6 and access to electoral-roll databases.The ECI said the SIR order issued on June 24, 2025, covering all states and Union territories, was approved unanimously. It also said the schedules for subsequent phases were issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission.Earlier in the day, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath also criticised the Congress and its allies over their attacks on the Election Commission and the SIR.“Congress and its allies should apologise to the constitutional institutions of the country and to the people for their actions,” Adityanath said.He said the SIR was not being conducted for the first time and pointed to earlier exercises carried out in 1952, 1957, 1961, 1965-66 and 2003.“Despite all this, the kind of uproar that the Congress, Samajwadi Party, RJD and other parties have created over the SIR this time is extremely unfortunate,” he added.Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also criticised the opposition over its demand for Kumar’s resignation. He alleged that Congress and its allies question the credibility of the Election Commission and EVMs after losing elections.“We are seeing what is happening. When the Congress wins in Telangana, Karnataka, Himachal Pradesh and Kerala, the Opposition does not comment on the Election Commission,” Shinde added.The political row comes amid continuing scrutiny of the Election Commission’s handling of the SIR. Opposition parties, including the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT), have demanded Kumar’s resignation.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi had alleged that the 2024 lok sabha and assembly elections were “all rigged” chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar must resign immediately, rahul said. Rijiju: “it is not appropriate to amplify rahul gandhi's remarks in the public sphere, as it would send the wrong message to society” the political row comes amid continuing scrutiny of the election commission’s handling of the sir.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Sunday questioned the status of the inquiry into the violence in Leh, saying a year had passed since the incidents and that those responsible were yet to be held accountable. He also raised concerns over the pending legal cases and the compensation for those who were killed.Wangchuk said he had travelled to Delhi to draw attention to the unresolved issues surrounding the violence and his subsequent imprisonment in Jodhpur."I had to come to Delhi to inform the country that a year has passed since those incidents in Ladakh, incidents that led to my own imprisonment in Jodhpur. I want to ask: what became of the findings of the inquiry commission set up regarding those incidents? When will the officials, the Governor, the Lieutenant Governor, and the Home Minister, who ordered such actions, provide answers? The issue remains unresolved. Those who were martyred have not yet received appropriate and dignified compensation. Legal cases are still pending against people, and many are left in a wretched state. There is no accountability."Protests demanding statehood for Ladakh and safeguards under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution turned violent on September 24, 2025, leaving four people dead and several others injured. The Union Territory administration subsequently ordered a judicial inquiry into the incident.Wangchuk was detained under the National Security Act (NSA) two days after the violence and was released in March this year.On the Election Commission of India row, Wangchuk said he supported organisations and leaders raising concerns over the electoral process and accountability, while acknowledging that he could not personally participate in every movement."I always extend my moral support to all organizations and leaders raising such issues, issues that are entirely valid, such as cleaning up the election process and ensuring accountability. However, it is not possible for me to personally join every single movement. I hope the entire country will join in demanding this accountability to build a clean, transparent democracy."The remarks come amid a political row over reported objections by two Election Commissioners to decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition parties have demanded action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, a halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held.The BJP, however, has defended the Election Commission, with party spokesperson Sambit Patra saying that dissent within the poll panel was a sign of a “vibrant democracy”.
Article Summary: Sonam wangchuk questions inquiry into leh violence and his subsequent imprisonment in jodhpur. Wangchuk said he had travelled to delhi to draw attention to the unresolved issues surrounding the violence. He also raised concerns over the pending legal cases and the compensation for those who were killed.
